5.12
Chunking Engine
Large documents cannot be directly indexed because language models and embedding
models have token limitations.
Therefore, every uploaded document is divided into
smaller semantic units called chunks.
The Intelligent Research Assistant implements three chunking strategies.
5.12.1
Fixed Size Chunking
In this approach, documents are divided into chunks containing a fixed number of tokens
with overlapping content between adjacent chunks.
Advantages include:
• Simple implementation
• Uniform chunk size
• Faster indexing
• Reduced context loss through overlap
5.12.2
Recursive Chunking
Recursive chunking attempts to split documents at natural boundaries.
The separator hierarchy is:
1. Paragraph
2. Newline
3. Sentence
4. Word
This strategy preserves contextual information better than fixed-size chunking.
5.12.3
Semantic Chunking
Semantic chunking groups sentences according to their semantic similarity.
The Sentence Transformer embedding model computes sentence embeddings, and con-
secutive sentences with high cosine similarity are grouped into the same chunk.
Advantages include:
• Better semantic coherence
